summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with acute-on-chronic left upper quadrant abdominal pain near her G-tube site, worsened over two weeks. Evaluation showed no signs of infection, obstruction, or free air on imaging. The pain was attributed to her known marginal ulcer, and she responded well to IV pain control with Dilaudid. Tube feeds were restarted to prevent hypoglycemia, and ulcer prophylaxis was continued. She was transitioned to liquid oxycodone for discharge and advised to follow up with pain management and GI for a planned EGD. The patient was discharged home in stable condition.
problems: Chronic gastrojejunal ulcer without mention of hemorrhage or perforation, without mention of obstruction
Unspecified disorder of pancreatic internal secretion
Personal history of Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus
